`Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:132456
Court No. - 68

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 15160 of 2024
Applicant :- Sahil Safaikarmi

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Dhirendra Kumar Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
This is the third bail application on behalf of the applicant.
The first and second bail application was rejected by Co-ordinate Bench (Hon'ble Deepak Verma, J.) of this Court vide orders dated 16.8.2022 and 8.5.2023, respectively.
The case is being heard by this Bench as after being released by Hon'ble Deepak Verma, J. and as per the Roster of Hon'ble The Chief Justice dated 5.8.2024.

2. Heard Sri Dhirendra Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri R.P. Patel,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.68 of 2022, under Section 376-E I.P.C., Police Station- Kotwali City, District- Mirzapur, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text:
PROSECUTION STORY:
4. The victim had gone for her examination to the District Government Hospital, Mirzapur on 7.5.2022.

The doctor had referred her for further examination at the District Women Hospital,
Mirzapur but in the intervening night at about 09:00 p.m. she suffered certain inconvenience and went to the toilet, whereby the applicant is stated to have entered it forcibly and committed rape with her.

After returning of her husband, the victim is stated to have informed him of the incident,
as such the FIR was instituted on 10.5.2022.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
5. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
6. The FIR is delayed by about three days and there is no proper explanation of the said delay caused.
7. The victim has not sustained any injuries whatsoever, as such the allegations are per se false.

8. The victim was examined as prosecution witness in court and she has reiterated the allegations levelled in the FIR, but at the time of her cross-examination by the public prosecutor she has categorically denied regarding the applicant being the assailant or the person who had committed rape with her.
9. She has categorically stated that she was told that the name of the assailant was Sahil but the person who is in court and stood for identification in the dock of the court is not the same person Sahil, as such the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case.
10. The statement of PW-2 is hearsay evidence, which is not admissible in Evidence Act.
11. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.

The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
12.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.

The applicant is languishing in jail since 11.5.2022,
as such more than two years have passed since incarceration.
The fundamental rights of the applicant enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India stand violated.
The applicant is ready to cooperate with trial.

In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE/OPPOSITE PARTY 13.

The bail application has been opposed on the ground that the victim has reiterated the allegations levelled in the FIR and in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: CONCLUSION:
14. Due to callous attitude or some other reason, the public prosecutor did not care to get the applicant identified in dock at the time of examination-in-chief.
The said act of the public prosecutor is deprecated as the applicant was very much available in court on the date of examination-in-chief.
15. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

16. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
17.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that ?bail is a rule and jail is an exception?.
18. Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
19. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

20. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

21. Let the applicant- Sahil Safaikarmi involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to Sahil Safaikarmi vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152392171/
3 treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

sentences.text: 22. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

23. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
